title: Icosapent ethyl with statin therapy for reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in people with raised triglycerides
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
journal: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, technology appraisal guidance TA805
authorConflicts: Committee members declare interests and are excluded from the appraisal if a conflict is found; declarations are posted in meeting minutes, not read.
result: Icosapent ethyl is recommended as an option for reducing the risk of cardiovascular events in adults with a high risk of cardiovascular events, raised fasting triglycerides (1.7 mmol/litre or above) and statin treatment, only if they have established cardiovascular disease and LDL cholesterol above 1.04 mmol/litre and below or equal to 2.60 mmol/litre; it is unlikely to be cost effective for primary prevention and is not recommended for it. The company provided the clinical evidence from REDUCE-IT, whose placebo group took 4 g of light mineral oil a day. The committee concluded that the relative effect of icosapent ethyl was uncertain because of the potential negative effect of the mineral oil placebo, noted that STRENGTH, with a corn oil placebo, did not show the same magnitude of benefit, concluded that the mechanism of action is not fully understood, and considered scenarios reducing the treatment effect by 1.5% to 3%.
